**3\. Register content of Capstone Project**  
**(\*) 3.1. Capstone Project name:**  
**3.1.1. English: *AI-assisted emergency dispatch system with vision-language-based hazard classification and severity scoring***  
**3.1.2. Vietnamese: *Hệ thống điều phối cứu hộ khẩn cấp thời gian thực ứng dụng AI phân loại mức độ nguy hiểm sự cố***

**(\*) 3.2. Main proposal content (including result and product)**

**a) Context:**

Within High-Tech Parks (HTP) and Industrial Parks (IP), operational risks remain high due to large concentrations of manufacturing plants, warehouses, and thousands of on-site workers. Two critical emergency categories that directly threaten human life and factory assets are **Fires** (workshop fires, electrical short circuits) and **Accidents** (internal transport collisions). In addition, high volumes of container trucks and commuter vehicles during peak shift transitions frequently cause localized **traffic congestion** at security checkpoints or main thoroughfares, hindering the prompt arrival of internal rescue vehicles.

Currently, incident reporting and emergency coordination within these parks rely heavily on direct phone calls to the internal security control room or communication via two-way radios. Workers often describe scene locations vaguely (e.g., near workshop X, gate Y), while dispatch operators manually assign patrol or rescue units based on personal familiarity rather than real-time vehicle locations and personnel availability. This results in delayed emergency responses, prolonged traffic gridlocks that disrupt supply logistics, and no real-time status visibility for either the reporting workers or the park management once units are deployed.

Furthermore, collaboration between the operations center and field patrol/rescue units lacks a centralized digital interface displaying precise GPS coordinates, incident severity levels, and congestion-free routes. Park authorities lack centralized data to evaluate response times, coverage, and resource dispatch efficiency.

This project proposes a lightweight, real-time coordination platform connecting workers/citizens, the Park Security & Incident Command Center, and internal mobile rescue/patrol units on a shared geolocation-based workflow (GIS). It integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to automatically classify hazards and score severity for **fires and accidents**, supplemented by a utility feature allowing workers to quickly report **traffic congestion hotspots** to optimize dispatch routing and road clearance.

**b) Proposed Solutions:**

The system is scoped around the closed-loop internal incident management and dispatch process within an Industrial/High-Tech Park, designed for complete execution by a 5-member team within a single capstone term. It includes 3 core implemented modules and 2 extended research directions:

*Core Areas (implemented in the capstone):*

* **Citizen/Worker Incident & Traffic Reporting:** One-touch SOS button for immediate reporting of Fires and Accidents with automatic GPS capture, scene photo/video attachment, and live tracking of responding units, alongside an auxiliary reporting flow for internal traffic bottlenecks.  
* **Command Center Dispatch & Monitoring:** Human-in-the-loop AI-assisted incident verification, severity assessment (Levels 1–3 for accidents and fires), nearest-available unit dispatch, and a real-time live map showing all units alongside reported congestion points.  
* **Rescue & Security Staff Mobile Operations:** Instant push notifications with high-priority audible alarms, turn-by-turn navigation to incident scenes, live operational status updates, and digital closure reporting with photo evidence upon resolving the incident.

**c) Functional Requirements:**  
The platform supports four primary user roles:

*Citizen / Internal Worker (Mobile Client):*

* One-Touch SOS Button: Automatically captures GPS coordinates and launches the camera to capture scene photos/videos for immediate reporting of **Fires** or **Accidents**.  
* Auxiliary Traffic Reporting: Submit reports on **internal traffic congestion / bottlenecks** with an optional brief note and photo (*no severity scoring applied*).  
* Track live location and Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) of assigned rescue/patrol units on an interactive map.  
* Receive real-time push notifications when reports are verified, units are dispatched, and scenes are cleared.  
* View personal incident reporting history on the device.  
   *Command Center Operator (Web Dashboard):*

* Real-time Live Map: Visualizes all internal patrol/rescue teams by operational status (Available, En Route, On Scene) alongside active traffic congestion markers.  
* Incident Queue: Displays pending accident and fire reports ranked by AI-recommended severity scores (Levels 1–3) with detected hazard tags (\#Fire, \#Accident) for operator verification prior to dispatch.  
* Receive and visualize reported traffic congestion points on the park map to warn dispatchers and guide response teams.  
* Semi-automated dispatching (one-click or drag-and-drop) to assign the nearest available internal rescue unit within a configurable radius.  
* Close incidents once field units submit digital closure reports.  
   *Rescue & Security Staff (Mobile Client):*

* Receive push notifications with prominent sound alerts upon new emergency assignment.  
* View turn-by-turn navigation to incident locations while identifying reported traffic jams to choose optimal routes.  
* Update operational status throughout the rescue workflow (Accepted, En Route, On Scene, Completed/Resolved).  
* Submit a digital incident closure report with photo evidence of scene clearance or medical handover.  
   *System Administrator (Back-office):*

* Manage directories of guard posts, patrol units, mini fire engines, and emergency rescue equipment (Status: Available / Maintenance).  
* Configure automated escalation rules: if a critical emergency (Level 3 fire/accident or total traffic paralysis) is not accepted within a specified threshold (e.g., 3–5 minutes), alert senior park security management immediately.  
* Manage user accounts and role-based permissions (Operator, Rescue Staff, Administrator).  
   *AI Module:*

* **AI-1 Hazard & Traffic Classification & Severity Scoring (Core AI Module):** Utilizes a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL API) to analyze submitted media, automatically classifying core emergency hazards into categories such as \#Fire and \#Accident while assigning a severity rating from **Level 1 to Level 3**. For the auxiliary traffic feature, the model detects the \#Traffic\_Jam tag to display map alerts without calculating severity levels. Evaluated against a benchmarked test dataset using standard classification metrics.

**d) Non-Functional Requirements:**

* **Performance:** Incident reports and unit status updates must synchronize with the Command Center dashboard within 1–3 seconds over a stable network.  
* **Scalability:** Capable of handling concurrent fire/accident reports, traffic updates, and real-time tracking streams across the designated industrial park pilot zone.  
* **Availability & Recovery:** Mobile applications feature offline report caching to queue and re-send data automatically upon network reconnection, backed by service health monitoring.  
* **Security:** Strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and encrypted data transmission (HTTPS/WSS).  
* **Privacy:** Protection of workers' phone numbers and personal location histories, restricted solely to authorized operational personnel.  
* **Data Integrity:** Complete lifecycle state auditing for every incident, recording timestamps, assigned personnel, and closure actions.  
* **Media Safety:** File type validation and payload size limits on media uploads prior to AI model processing.  
* **Usability:** Mobile interfaces optimized for one-handed operation during emergency stress; dashboard designed for standard desktop control-room screens.  
* **Maintainability:** Modular backend architecture, documented REST/WebSocket APIs, version control, and automated tests for dispatch workflows and AI processing.

**e) Theory & Practical:**

* Software requirements engineering and workflow modeling for internal emergency and traffic response (BPMN, Use Cases).  
* Real-time event-driven architecture using WebSocket for live map visualization and instantaneous dispatch signaling.  
* Geospatial queries to identify nearest available rescue/patrol units within industrial park boundaries.  
* Applied computer vision: integrating and evaluating Vision-Language Model APIs for multi-label hazard classification and severity scoring.  
* Mobile-first responsive frontend development (for workers and field staff) and Web Dashboard engineering for dispatch operators.  
* Relational database schema design (PostgreSQL) for incident management, unit tracking, and state history logging.  
* Functional, integration, and performance testing methodologies for real-time systems, along with empirical AI evaluation protocols.  
* Team code collaboration via Git and containerized deployment using Docker.

**f) Products (Expected Deliverables):**

* Mobile application (Web and Mobile App) for Workers/Citizens: One-touch SOS (fire/accident), traffic jam reporting, and live rescue tracking.  
* Mobile application for Rescue & Security Staff: Immediate dispatch reception, park navigation, and digital closure reporting.  
* Web Dashboard for Command Center Operators: Real-time map, traffic hotspot tracking, prioritized incident queue, and dispatch console.  
* Back-office administration module: Directory management for rescue assets and escalation configuration.  
* Fully integrated AI-1 module for hazard classification, traffic identification, and severity scoring (Levels 1–3), accompanied by an empirical evaluation report.  
* Backend services, real-time WebSocket communication infrastructure, and database.  
* Software engineering documentation: SRS, Use Case specifications, database diagrams, API documentation, test plans, and user manuals.  
* Complete source code, test reports, and a demonstrable deployed prototype.

**g) Proposed Tasks:**

* **TP1 \- Business Analysis & System Design (Whole team):** Survey internal park emergency and traffic procedures; define four actor roles; construct SRS, UI/UX designs, database schemas, API specs, and software architecture.  
* **TP2 \- SOS Reporting App & Core AI Module:** Develop the worker mobile reporting client (SOS for fire/accident, traffic reporting); integrate Qwen2.5-VL for hazard classification and severity scoring (Levels 1–3); conduct model evaluations.  
* **TP3 \- Command Center Dispatch & Live Map:** Build the Web Dashboard, real-time Live Map via WebSocket, prioritized incident queue, and nearest-unit dispatch algorithms.  
* **TP4 \- Rescue Staff App & Admin Module:** Build the field staff mobile client (job acceptance, navigation, digital closure) and the back-office escalation and asset management module.  
* **TP5 \- Integration, Testing & Delivery (Whole team):** Conduct end-to-end integration across all clients, backend, and AI modules; execute functional, security, and performance testing; containerize via Docker, deploy the prototype, and finalize deliverables.

**3.3. Research Information**

**a. Research Problem**

* **RQ1:** How accurately and efficiently can a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL) classify industrial park emergency hazards (fires, accidents) and detect traffic congestion, as well as score severity levels (Levels 1–3) from user-submitted media compared to human-labeled ground truth?  
* **RQ2:** How does a Nearest-Available dispatch heuristic compare to a Load-Aware heuristic (accounting for existing unit task loads and transit times) regarding average response time and workload balance across internal rescue units in an industrial park?  
* **RQ3:** To what extent does human-in-the-loop AI-assisted verification reduce operator time-to-dispatch compared to a traditional manual verification baseline in an industrial park context?

**b. Research Objectives**

* Design and evaluate an AI-assisted pipeline using a Vision-Language Model tailored for classifying fire/accident emergencies, detecting traffic congestion, and scoring severity (Levels 1–3).  
* Implement and benchmark two dispatch heuristics (Nearest-Available vs. Load-Aware) under simulated high-incident operational workloads within an industrial park.  
* Quantify the reduction in operator dispatch decision time achieved through AI-assisted incident pre-filtering and prioritization compared to manual triage.

**c. Research Scope & Methodology**

The research scope is strictly confined to software-based decision support for incident classification and internal rescue dispatching within an Industrial/High-Tech Park; it excludes emergency vehicle hardware modifications or external municipal traffic signal control.

Core evaluation metrics:

* Classification accuracy and F1-score for fire, accident, and traffic congestion tags.  
* Severity scoring agreement (Levels 1–3) between the AI model and human evaluators using Weighted Cohen's Kappa.  
* Mean incident-to-dispatch response time across comparative dispatch heuristics.  
* Workload variance and balance among internal rescue/patrol units.  
* Operator time-to-dispatch: AI-assisted workflow versus manual baseline.  
   Experiments will utilize a labeled validation dataset of photos/videos depicting factory fires, electrical short circuits, industrial accidents, vehicle collisions, and internal traffic jams, combined with controlled dispatch simulations to assess operational performance.

**d. Expected Scientific Contribution**

* A validated Vision-Language Model pipeline customized for emergency classification and severity assessment of industrial park fires and accidents, benchmarked against human annotations.  
* Comparative empirical analysis of resource dispatch heuristics in a closed-campus operational environment.  
* Quantitative operational evidence establishing the response-time benefits of human-in-the-loop AI verification over traditional manual dispatch methods.
